## Body

Statusline identity needs the nearest harness host, not any matching ancestor. The earlier inherited-identity note covers a paneless child's environment; #240 adds the important counterexample where the registered parent's PID really IS on the ancestry chain. A regression with an unrelated foreign PID cannot catch that defect. Model registered A -> separate unregistered B -> shell -> statusline, plus direct B -> statusline: neither may display A; B's own binding and A's own statusline must still work.

The repaired guard stops at the first recognized copilot/node/claude/codex/omp/bun/pi host and compares that host's PID AND recorded start. Shell wrappers are traversable; an outer matching host never counts after an inner host. Keep invocation and registration aligned: the managed script execs pij-rs, and native registration selects the nearest Copilot ancestor, not its outer node launcher. Our bounded live ancestry observation was consistent with a native copilot child of a node launcher and direct pij-rs children; it did not inspect argv or prove every helper topology. Do not invent a helper false negative without establishing normal use, or turn this display-correctness guard into same-user isolation work.

Process-name normalization is part of correctness. Linux /proc/<pid>/exe appends " (deleted)" after an executable is replaced; strip exactly one trailing suffix, consistently with registration, or an otherwise live host becomes invisible. macOS reads the existing checked ProcBSDShortInfo parent/name structure; its 16-byte name field includes NUL, and the recognized short host names fit. These paths are in-process, with no new ps, tmux, shell or PATH launch.

Cost wording must distinguish zero NEW launches from the existing CLI invocation and exceptional git fallback. Direct ancestry needs two parent/name observations and one start observation; the actual ceiling is self plus 64 ancestors (65 observations), not 64 total. Linux adds an executable-link read per inspected process; macOS gets parent/name in the same syscall. spawn_sites.rs excludes CLI launches: its green result is not proof of the statusline's launch rate.

Closure receipts: #240 S240-001 closed at 520e5d196305eb61a668bba93257719f0095272f, final verdict commit ed23c5b85266d80724c5a94171debc41b5cedb2f; requester reports merge 2d5b1a9c. Source at that reviewed head: crates/cli/src/statusline.rs:326-408; statusline_tests.rs:666-846; crates/harnesses/src/proc.rs:339-399,717-726; .copilot/extensions/pij/store.mjs:435-436,2512-2544; harness/scripts/copilot-statusline-pij.sh:12; crates/daemon/src/registration.rs:2043-2052. The named nested-host and Linux deleted-suffix regressions passed in final-head CI, as did receiver recovery-field removal and never-renewed diagnosis assertions (crates/daemon/src/http/native_tests.rs:2633-2663,2881-2889).

Do not upgrade the proof grade at handoff: macOS was source-reviewed, not compiled here; no local builds/tests ran. After-install/bounce own/foreign/nested statusline and lease lapse/recovery checks, paired same-PID spawn counters, 20-second spawn-rate, and CPU/RSS receipts remained owed in the final verdict. The <=64-read cost prose correction is a named nonblocking C34 follow-up, not grounds for a third round.
